pasta-whole-grain-with-tomato-based-sauc.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and pieces of poultry is a home recipe created in 2023. Whole grain pasta retains most of the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than traditional white pasta. The tomato sauce, made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, and aromatic herbs, gives the dish a bright flavor, while tender poultry adds extra protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains twice as much fiber as regular white pasta.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
The poultry used is often free‑range, increasing its omega‑3 fatty acid content.
Traditional Italian marinara sauce is a common base for similar tomato sauces.
Making the sauce at home lets you control the amount of salt and sugar.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and blood sugar regulation.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce contain lycopene, which helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than white pasta, beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Protein from poultry
items.content: Lean poultry offers high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the whole grain pasta and tomato sauce supply B1, B3, and B6 vitamins, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake moderate.

items.title: Potential poultry pathogens
items.content: Poultry must be cooked thoroughly to avoid risks of salmonella and campylobacter.

items.title: Tomato acidity
items.content: People with acid reflux may experience discomfort from the acidic tomato sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta until al dente, then toss with hot tomato sauce and sautéed poultry pieces. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or oregano. Serve with a green salad or vegetable side dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry whole grain pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Keep cooked sauce and finished dishes in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Peanut oil is extracted from the seeds of the peanut plant (Arachis hypogaea). It has a light nutty aroma, pale yellow color, and a high smoke point, making it popular for frying and cooking in Asian cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut oil is a staple in traditional Chinese and Thai cooking for deep‑frying.
Compared with many other vegetable oils, peanut oil contains a relatively high proportion of monounsaturated fats.
There are two main types: refined (neutral flavor, very high smoke point) and unrefined (strong nutty flavor, lower smoke point).
Peanut oil is also used in cosmetics as a moisturizing ingredient.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support cardiovascular health and help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Contains phytosterols
items.content: Phytosterols may contribute to lowering blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: Its high calorie density and healthy fats make it a good energy source for active individuals.

items.title: Contains antioxidant compounds
items.content: Polyphenols in peanut oil help combat inflammation.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: People with peanut allergy can experience severe reactions even to small amounts of the oil.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of its energy density, the oil should be used in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Omega‑6 fatty acids
items.content: Excessive omega‑6 intake without adequate omega‑3 balance may promote inflammatory processes.

items.title: Trans fats from improper heating
items.content: Overheating or poor storage can lead to the formation of small amounts of trans fats.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Peanut oil is suitable for frying, baking, making sauces, marinades, and Asian dishes. It can be added to salads, smoothies, or used as a noodle dressing. Unrefined oil is best when a strong nutty flavor is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep it in the refrigerator to slow oxidation. Discard the oil if it develops a rancid smell.
